label: Тебя
description: Object-form sentences that train how 'you' behaves after verbs and prepositions.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Object pronoun after a verb. 'Тебя' is the accusative object form of 'ты', and 'видит' is third-person singular. 'Из окна' adds a genitive source phrase and shows how the pronoun shifts when it is no longer the subject.

Strategic focus: Simple transitive verb. 'Тебя' is the direct object of 'ждёт', a third-person singular form. 'У входа' adds a genitive location, making this a common real-life sentence about meeting up.

Strategic focus: Plural subject plus object pronoun. 'Они' forces the plural verb 'знают', while 'тебя' stays the accusative object form. The adverb 'хорошо' lets the contrast between subject and object roles ring clearly.

Strategic focus: Object pronoun with location. 'Тебя' is the accusative object being waited for, and 'дома' adds an everyday location. The adverb 'уже' combines verb government with a stable place word in natural speech.

Strategic focus: Direct object in a family sentence. 'Тебя' is the accusative person being called, and 'зовёт' is a high-frequency third-person verb. 'На кухню' adds a destination that makes the line easy to remember.
Strategic focus: Object pronoun in a plural environment. 'Тебя' remains the accusative object form, while 'ждут' is plural agreeing with 'друзья'. 'У двери' adds a practical genitive spatial phrase.
Strategic focus: Preposition plus the genitive object form. 'Без' governs the genitive, and 'тебя' follows it naturally. 'Мы не начнём' gives the line a real conversational shape with a future verb.
Strategic focus: Relevance through a preposition. 'Для' governs the genitive 'тебя' to express relevance, and 'это' introduces the topic. 'Очень важно' closes the line with a natural evaluation.
Strategic focus: Motion toward the listener. 'К' governs the dative 'тебе' to mark direction, and 'пришли' is plural past tense. 'Гости' and 'сегодня' keep the scene vivid and practical.

Strategic focus: Prepositional phrase with the instrumental form. 'С' governs the instrumental 'тобой', and 'рядом' marks closeness. 'Сидит учитель' gives a clear spatial relation that is easy to picture.

Strategic focus: Possession construction. 'У тебя есть' is the standard Russian possession pattern, with 'у' governing the genitive 'тебя'. 'Интересная книга' is the possessed item and contrasts with English-style ownership.

Strategic focus: Negation of possession. 'У тебя нет' is the negative possession pattern, and 'времени' shows the genitive after 'нет'. The adverb 'совсем' makes this one of the most practical everyday lines in Russian.

Strategic focus: Preposition with the genitive object form. 'После' governs the genitive, so 'тебя' follows it naturally. 'Пришёл новый сосед' gives a concrete clause that keeps the sentence grounded.

Strategic focus: Fixed prepositional phrase. 'Перед' governs the instrumental 'тобой' to mark position, and 'лежит' provides a stable visual action. 'Важное письмо' is a compact object that fits the scene.

Strategic focus: Object pronoun plus prepositional complement. 'Тебя' is the accusative person being asked, and 'спрашивает' is a common interaction verb. 'О работе' shows how a verb can add a second prepositional target.

Strategic focus: Object pronoun with an adverb. 'Тебя' is the accusative object being listened to, and 'слушают' is plural agreeing with the subject. 'Очень внимательно' makes the sentence feel alive and natural.

Strategic focus: Identity question. 'Тебя зовут' is a fixed naming construction with 'тебя' as the accusative object, and 'как' opens the question. There is no subject pronoun the way English uses one, making this a crucial survival phrase.

Strategic focus: Past absence. 'Тебя не было' is the common absence pattern, with 'тебя' in the genitive after 'не было'. 'Вчера' and 'дома' keep it concrete, showing how Russian expresses absence without an English-style subject.

Strategic focus: Reversed-feeling expectation. 'Тебя' is the accusative person who is awaited, while 'ждёт' is singular agreeing with the real subject 'работа'. The adjective 'серьёзная' shows how roles can feel reversed from English.

Strategic focus: Preposition plus a past event. 'Без' governs the genitive 'тебя', and 'встреча уже началась' gives a natural event clause. This is a very useful real-world line for explaining an absence.
